items.stem: A fast neural-network emulator replaces an expensive physics simulation. What is the main risk when using it for new parameter values?

options.text: It may extrapolate unreliably outside the range of its training data
options.rationale: Correct: emulators are trustworthy mainly within their training domain and can fail on extrapolation.

options.text: It will always be slower than the original simulation
options.rationale: Emulators are used precisely because they are faster.

options.text: It cannot represent any physical behaviour
options.rationale: A trained emulator can reproduce in-domain behaviour well.

options.text: It eliminates the need to understand the physics
options.rationale: Interpreting and validating results still requires physics understanding.

items.explanation: Correct: emulators are trustworthy mainly within their training domain and can fail on extrapolation.

items.stem: Which TWO practices are essential before an AI-flagged anomaly is treated as a physics discovery? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validating the model against known signals and simulated backgrounds
options.rationale: Correct: validation against known cases is essential before claiming discovery.

options.text: Quantifying and reporting the statistical significance and uncertainty
options.rationale: Correct: significance and uncertainty must be established, not just a flag.

options.text: Announcing the result immediately to establish priority
options.rationale: Premature announcement without verification is irresponsible.

options.text: Removing all events the model is unsure about to clean the plot
options.rationale: Selectively discarding data biases the result.

items.explanation: Correct: validation against known cases is essential before claiming discovery.

items.stem: Why is calibration of predicted uncertainties important when AI informs a physics decision?

options.text: A model whose confidence does not match its true error rate can mislead decisions
options.rationale: Correct: well-calibrated uncertainties let decision-makers weigh AI outputs correctly.
Calibration concerns reliability of uncertainty, not speed.

options.text: Calibration guarantees the prediction is correct
options.rationale: Calibration aligns stated confidence with accuracy; it does not guarantee correctness.

options.text: Uncertainty is irrelevant if accuracy is high
options.rationale: Even accurate models need honest uncertainty for rare or novel cases.

items.explanation: Correct: well-calibrated uncertainties let decision-makers weigh AI outputs correctly.
